rationale: Record what this turn's repair attempt established about the Node-wrapper proposal lead and keep it unresolved. The source account is unchanged; the new information is diagnostic: observations of the wrapped node must be read through the node's own status channel (or from inside its goroutine), because the draft probe read raft fields straight from the test goroutine while the run loop was mutating them, and one snapshot even showed an impossible pair (committed 3 with last index 0). The native run also failed to show the wrapped node processing the leader's initial append within the wait window, so the harness itself, not only the observation point, needs repair before an execution can be requested.

interpretations.rationale: The source account stands as recorded: node.run closes the proposal channel when an applied configuration change removes the local node from Progress (the guard requires that the node was in Progress before, is not after, and appears in neither Voters nor VotersOutgoing) and re-opens it only in the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead with a leader known, while applying a change that adds the node back takes the okBefore=false path; Node.Propose then selects on a nil channel and returns only through the caller's context or the node's done channel. The draft probe assurance_node_proposal_test.go aims to compare Propose before the removal, after the re-add and after a leadership change, and this turn was spent repairing it. Two problems were found and neither is yet fixed. First, the probe's observations were taken by reading the wrapped node's raft fields from the test goroutine while the node's run loop was mutating them; one snapshot reported committed_index 3 together with last_index 0, which is not a state the node can be in, so those readings are not admissible. The repair is to take every snapshot through the node's status channel (node.Status, which is executed inside the run loop) and to keep only the app-visible endpoints (Propose's return value and duration, the leader's own log index) from the test goroutine. Second, the native run did not show the wrapped node processing the leader's initial append within a three second wait: the node reported term 0 and no leader while the leader's own log had advanced, and it only reported term 1 later, after the configuration-change pump. Since the premise of the comparison (a member that knows the leader) cannot be established with the current harness, no execution is requested and no defect is claimed.
counterevidence: The Node.Propose documentation states that proposals can be lost without notice and that ensuring retries is the caller's job (node.go:138-140), so a blocked or failed proposal on a re-added node overlaps with behaviour callers are warned about; the specific claim to test remains the unavailability of the channel while the node is a member and a leader is known.
The observed blocks in both native runs occurred in states whose premise could not be confirmed (no leader visible to the reader), so they do not establish the removal as the cause.
limitations: No retained receipt exists for this probe, and the harness must first be repaired: snapshots through the node's status channel, and a pump that demonstrably drives the wrapped node through the bootstrap append before any configuration change is proposed.
The harness drives a wrapped node against a bare raft rather than two application-driven nodes, so the wrapper's asynchronous ready/advance contract is exercised on one side only.

Whether an application is expected to keep proposing through a node that has been removed and re-added is itself part of the question; the library's own comment calls the current mechanism unsound rather than documenting an intended semantics.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal channel is closed by the removal guard and restored only by a leadership change with a leader known.
With a nil proposal channel Propose blocks until the caller's context or the node's done channel fires.
